title: Gretel's Gingerbread Pear Cake
tagline: Treacle-black, pumpkin-soft, and built to lure children. Politely.

ingredients.qty: 175g, softened, plus extra for the tin
2 tsp ground ginger and 1 tsp ground cinnamon

steps: Heat the oven to 170°C fan. Grease and line a 22cm round tin. Melt 50g butter, 75g sugar and 1 tbsp treacle in a pan until bubbling, then pour into the tin.
Lay the pears cut side down over the toffee, then scatter the chestnuts into the gaps.
Beat the remaining 125g butter, 100g sugar and 2 tbsp treacle until fluffy. Add the eggs one at a time, beating well after each.
Fold in the flour and spices, then the pumpkin purée and milk, until just combined. Spoon over the pears and level gently.
Bake for 45 to 50 minutes, until a skewer comes out clean. Cool in the tin for 10 minutes, then turn out while still warm.
Serve warm with crème fraîche or custard. It keeps well for three days and gets stickier, which is the point.
image_prompt: A round upside-down gingerbread cake turned out onto a dark slate plate, glossy near-black treacle toffee glaze pooling around it, three caramelised pear halves on top studded with chopped chestnuts, one slice cut to show a dark, moist, spiced pumpkin crumb, a spoonful of crème fraîche beside it.
alt_text: A glossy treacle-glazed upside-down pear gingerbread cake on a dark plate, with one slice cut to show the moist spiced crumb.
caption_hook: Hansel left breadcrumbs. Gretel, frankly, should have left cake. This one's pear, chestnut and a lot of treacle. Who's brave enough to follow the trail?
